newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - S&P 500 seen poised for pullback.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - S&P 500 seen poised for pullback.

text.p: The Standard & Poor's 500 index has flashed negative technical signals and is poised for a short-term pullback, technical analysts said on Tuesday.

The broad U.S. stock market gauge peaked on February 18 at a record closing level of 816.29. But after a decline, two subsequent rally attempts in late February and early March failed to top the record summit.
The index was down four points at 792 in afternoon trading on Tuesday. Analysts said a break below the 785 level could signal a near-term retreat for the index.
"If we violate that trough, that would begin a short-term downtrend for the S&P," said Peter Green, vice president technical research Gruntal & Co.
On Monday S&P 500 index fell to 783 during a midsession selloff but recovered to close at 796, which analysts cited as a positive move.
But John Wosczyna, market strategist at Roney & Co, said he saw little support at 785 for the S&P.
"My bet would be a break in the next couple of days," he said.

Citing loss of support from groups of stocks, including energy and technology, whose momentum had driven the market to highs, Wosczyna said he expected the S&P 500 to be in the 740-to-750 level by the second or third week of April.
Alan Newman, technical analyst at H.D. Brous & Co, cited a trendline starting at the index's low around 625 last July and ending around the 780-785 level.
"Once that breaks down you'll probably have a lot of people fleeing to the sidelines," he said.
Newman said he expected the index to break below the trendline and the S&P 500 to be down about 20 points in "possibly as little as a week."
But he said he expected some support to emerge around the 770-to-775 level as bargain hunters stepped before what he said he expects to be further deterioration.
